findings.title: Journal search crashes (500) on an apostrophe or quote; SQL built by string interpolation
findings.where: GET /api/journal (q param); Journal page and plant detail journal
findings.steps: Sign in, go to the Journal page, and type a word containing an apostrophe into the search box, e.g. "it's" (or any text with a single quote). Equivalent API call: GET /api/journal?q=it's
findings.expected: The search runs and shows matching entries (or an empty-state), or at worst rejects bad input with a 4xx. An ordinary apostrophe is normal text a gardener types.
findings.actual: The request returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error. The search term is substituted directly into the SQL with an f-string: clauses.append(f"(j.body LIKE '%{term}%' OR p.name LIKE '%{term}%')") in backend/routers/journal.py, so a single quote breaks the SQL. This is also a SQL-injection hole (the term is attacker-controlled and unparameterized). The repo already provides escape_like() and parameter binding in routers/common.py, which this code does not use.
findings.evidence: curl 'GET /api/journal?q=it%27s' returned 'Internal Server Error [500]'. Payloads containing a quote such as "' OR 1=1 --" also returned 500, confirming the term lands inside the SQL literal.

findings.title: Journal search treats % and _ as wildcards instead of literal characters
findings.expected: Searching for "%" should match only entries whose text actually contains a percent sign (or return no matches), not every entry.
findings.actual: Because the term is placed inside a LIKE pattern without escaping, % and _ act as SQL wildcards. Searching "%" returns all entries; "_" matches any single character. Users can't search for these literal characters.
findings.evidence: curl 'GET /api/journal?q=%25' returned the full list of entries rather than only those containing a percent sign.

findings.title: Journal page load/error state offers no retry
findings.where: Journal page (frontend/app/pages/journal.vue); also journal section of plant detail page
findings.steps: Cause the journal fetch to fail (e.g. search a quote to trigger the 500, or stop the API). Observe the error UI.
findings.expected: Per the resilience requirements, a page that loads data should present an error state with a retry control so the user can try again once the server is back, without reloading the page.
findings.actual: On failure the page only renders the AlertMessage text 'Could not load the journal.' There is no retry button; the user must reload. (The plant detail journal section shows the same alert-only pattern with no retry.)
findings.evidence: journal.vue renders only <AlertMessage v-if="loadError"> with no retry action; plant [id].vue similarly shows journalLoadError via AlertMessage only.
